tEn: The Changing Physics of Cybersecurity and Drug Development
tZh: 网络安全与药物研发的物理法则之变
sEn: OpenAI President Greg Brockman on AI generating new knowledge, solving century-old math problems, and why security spending should vastly outstrip software spending.
sZh: OpenAI 总裁 Greg Brockman 谈 AI 创造新知识、破解百年数学难题，以及为何安全支出应远超软件支出。

consensus.en: AI can now generate genuinely new knowledge, resolving century-old math problems.
consensus.zh: AI 现在能够生成真正的新知识，解决百年数学难题。

consensus.en: Humans must remain firmly in the driver's seat; AI should amplify human agency.
consensus.zh: 人类必须牢牢掌握方向盘；AI 应增强人类能动性。

consensus.en: Drug discovery is the most obvious area for AI to revolutionize, but data bottlenecks remain.
consensus.zh: 药物发现是 AI 最明显要革命的领域，但数据瓶颈依然存在。

consensus.en: The best UI is no UI; AI will dynamically generate interfaces tailored to each user's needs.
consensus.zh: 最好的 UI 是没有 UI；AI 将动态生成针对每个用户需求的界面。

consensus.en: We are in a defender's window; defenders must use frontier AI to find and fix vulnerabilities now.
consensus.zh: 我们正处于防御者窗口期；防御者必须现在就用前沿 AI 发现并修复漏洞。

consensus.en: Security spending should vastly outstrip software spending as software becomes cheap and ubiquitous.
consensus.zh: 随着软件变得廉价且无处不在，安全支出应远超软件支出。

contrarian.en: AI's math results show it can produce beautiful insights, not just incomprehensible proofs.
contrarian.zh: AI 的数学成果表明它能产生优美的洞见，而不仅仅是难以理解的证明。

contrarian.en: Humans are incredibly bad at biology; neural nets may crack biology's language from first principles.
contrarian.zh: 人类在生物学上非常糟糕；神经网络可能从第一性原理破解生物学的语言。

contrarian.en: Cyber spend should vastly outstrip software spend, reversing the traditional low-single-digit IT budget allocation.
contrarian.zh: 网络安全支出应远超软件支出，逆转传统上占 IT 预算低个位数的分配。

contrarian.en: AI lets us pay down tech debt in ways previously unthinkable, enabling formal verification of software security.
contrarian.zh: AI 让我们以前所未有的方式偿还技术债务，实现软件安全的形式化验证。

contrarian.en: Consumer and enterprise AI assistants will converge, blurring the traditional distinction between them.
contrarian.zh: 消费者和企业 AI 助手将融合，模糊它们之间的传统界限。

contrarian.en: Regulation should change quickly once AI proves better results, e.g., in clinical trials or self-driving cars.
contrarian.zh: 一旦 AI 证明能产生更好结果（如临床试验或自动驾驶），监管应迅速改变。

turns.en: Hi listeners, welcome back to No Priors. Today, Elad and I talk with Greg Brockman, the co-founder and president of OpenAI.
turns.zh: 嗨，听众朋友们，欢迎回到 No Priors。今天，我和 Elad 与 OpenAI 的联合创始人兼总裁 Greg Brockman 进行了对话。

turns.en: We discuss OpenAI's latest math results, Astra, and why Greg believes AI can now generate genuinely new knowledge. We get into drug discovery dots, and his case for why security spending should actually vastly outstrip software spending, which is quite a claim. Here's our conversation with Greg Brockman.
turns.zh: 我们讨论了 OpenAI 最新的数学成果、Astra，以及为什么 Greg 认为 AI 现在能够生成真正的新知识。我们谈到了药物发现的要点，以及他主张安全支出实际上应该远远超过软件支出，这是一个相当大胆的论断。以下是我们的对话。

turns.en: Greg, thanks so much for doing this.
turns.zh: Greg，非常感谢你接受这次访谈。

turns.en: Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: So, every week in AI feels like a year, and a lot's happened this week for OpenAI. You rolled out GPT-6 to over a billion people, which is pretty amazing. There's some really exciting news that you have on the math side. There's all sorts of things that undoubtedly are happening internally. What are you most excited about that's happening right now both at OpenAI and in the broader AI world?
turns.zh: 在 AI 领域，每周都感觉像过了一年，而本周 OpenAI 发生了很多事情。你们向超过十亿人推出了 GPT-6，这非常了不起。在数学方面，你们有一些非常令人兴奋的消息。毫无疑问，内部还发生着各种各样的事情。对于 OpenAI 内部以及更广泛的 AI 世界目前正在发生的事情，你最兴奋的是什么？

turns.en: Look, I think that in AI, I have this belief about how OpenAI operates: there's a cycling quote of it never gets easier, you just go faster. And I think that's very much what happens: there's just so much activity, and every time you think you're at peak impact and how things are happening, you realize that there's actually another level that's possible. And it's not just about any one company, it's not just about any one technology, it's really about we as a world and society are all coming together to adopt this technology, get the most out of it to improve everyone's lives.
turns.zh: 看，我认为在 AI 领域，我对 OpenAI 的运作方式有这样的信念：有一句自行车界的名言——它永远不会变得更容易，你只会骑得更快。我认为情况正是如此：活动如此之多，每次你认为自己处于影响力的顶峰，事情的发展方式，你意识到实际上还有另一个层次是可能的。这不仅仅是关于任何一家公司，也不仅仅是关于任何一项技术，而是关于我们作为世界和社会都在共同采用这项技术，最大限度地利用它来改善每个人的生活。

turns.en: And so, I think to me, the math results this week represent a real milestone. It's a real moment where if you think about the fundamental driver of human quality of life improving over the past thousand years, it's technology, it's scientific advancement. And I think that we now have the ability to massively accelerate scientific discovery. And there's always been this question of is AI actually able to come up with new knowledge? And at this point, it's just impossible to deny. It is definitively yes, possible. Now, there's still more to go. I think we're not yet coming up with whole brand new theories, but we are able to resolve these hundred-year-old math problems.
turns.zh: 所以，我认为本周的数学成果代表了一个真正的里程碑。这是一个真正的时刻：如果你思考过去一千年人类生活质量提高的根本驱动力，那就是技术，是科学进步。我认为我们现在有能力大规模加速科学发现。一直存在一个问题：AI 是否真的能够提出新知识？在这一点上，已经无法否认。答案绝对是肯定的，是可能的。现在，还有更多要做。我认为我们还没有提出全新的理论，但我们能够解决这些百年数学难题。

turns.en: And to me, the thing that's very exciting is it's not just about the machine just gives you an answer. It's really what can a human equipped with these tools achieve that was unthinkable before. And I think it's almost like the leverage of humans to do whatever you want to do, it's going way, way up. Now you can, if you have a math problem you want to go solve, you can solve it. But what about taking that same capability, applying it to biology? What about if you're a small business owner and you want to be able to operate your business well? That level of intelligence that's tuned for that domain, it's just going to mean that almost these unthinkable results that are aligned with your goals, with your desires, are now going to be within the reach of everyone. And that to me is so exciting.
turns.zh: 对我来说，非常令人兴奋的是，这不仅仅是机器给你一个答案。而是人类配备这些工具后能实现以前无法想象的事情。我认为这几乎就像人类的杠杆作用，无论你想做什么，它都在大幅提升。现在，如果你有一个数学问题想解决，你可以解决它。但把同样的能力应用到生物学上呢？如果你是一个小企业主，想要很好地经营你的业务呢？那种针对该领域调整的智能水平，将意味着几乎这些与你的目标、你的愿望一致的不可想象的结果，现在将触手可及。这对我来说太令人兴奋了。

turns.en: The rate of progress has been pretty amazing, too, because if I look at it, you used to have problems with arithmetic, right? And early models, I remember people complain, "Oh, why can't it do basic math?" And now you're solving these advanced theorems. As these things continue to advance and this starts to really impact areas of math, physics, materials, et cetera, and various applications, is there some need if these models get so smart to focus on how to communicate that effectively to people or how do you think about the actual communication side of this as you do a very advanced theorem? Because if you look at any field of math, only a very small number of people can ever really adjudicate a theorem that's produced by a person.
turns.zh: 进步的速度也非常惊人，因为如果我回顾一下，过去模型在算术上都有问题，对吧？早期的模型，我记得人们抱怨：“哦，为什么它不会做基础数学？”而现在你们在解决这些高级定理。随着这些事物继续进步，并开始真正影响数学、物理、材料等领域以及各种应用，如果这些模型变得如此聪明，是否有必要关注如何有效地向人们传达这一点，或者你如何看待实际的沟通方面，当你处理一个非常高级的定理时？因为如果你看任何数学领域，只有极少数人能够真正评判一个人产生的定理。

turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Right? And so you kind of have this specialization that happens.
turns.zh: 对吧？所以你就有了这种专业化。

turns.en: Well, and this by the way is something that has always been—I came from a math background. I thought I was going to be a mathematician and I was very inspired by mathematicians like Galois or Gauss. These people who were working on like a 100, 400 year time horizon. And I think there's something deeply beautiful about mathematics being about understanding the structure of the universe. And so it's not just about—and there's always these questions about is math invented or discovered? And in my mind, the beauty and the meaning of mathematics, it's not something that is objective in some sense. It's in the eye of the beholder. It's something that appeals to us and there is some math that's like physical laws and it's about simplicity and compression theory, complexity theory and all these things that are maybe more physics, but there's something that is also importantly human about it.
turns.zh: 嗯，顺便说一句，这一直是——我来自数学背景。我以为我会成为一名数学家，我深受伽罗瓦或高斯这样的数学家的启发。这些人在 100 年、400 年的时间跨度上工作。我认为数学的深刻之美在于理解宇宙的结构。所以这不仅仅是——而且总是有这些问题：数学是发明的还是发现的？在我看来，数学的美和意义，在某种意义上并不是客观的。它在观者的眼中。它是吸引我们的东西，有些数学像物理定律，关乎简单性和压缩理论、复杂性理论等等，这些可能更偏向物理，但其中也有重要的属于人的东西。

turns.en: And so to me it's not just about—I think a lot of the conversation about mathematics is not just about here's a proof, no one understands it, great, we resolved the problem. It's really about what are the insights that are derived and the thing that I think we will see—but I think that there's promising signs of life on—is that there's beautiful insights within the work that these AIs have done. And I think what we're seeing right now is that we published about almost 400 very important open problems that are now resolved and the mathematical community is going through all of that to look for insights. And if you read some of the things that people have posted, domain experts in these particular problems, they say that there's these almost very surprising ways of applying ideas or incredibly—wait, why did they use that result over here? And what's coming out is not these incomprehensible theorems or proofs, which by the way, there's a history of incomprehensible proofs in mathematics.
turns.zh: 所以对我来说，这不仅仅是——我认为很多关于数学的讨论不仅仅是这里有一个证明，没人理解它，太好了，我们解决了问题。这真的是关于推导出的见解是什么，我认为我们将看到——但我认为有希望的迹象——这些 AI 所做的工作中有美丽的见解。我认为我们现在看到的是，我们发表了大约 400 个非常重要的开放问题，现在已解决，数学界正在研究所有这些以寻找见解。如果你读一些人们发布的东西，这些特定问题的领域专家，他们说有这些几乎非常令人惊讶的应用想法的方式，或者令人难以置信——等等，为什么他们在这里使用了那个结果？而出来的不是这些不可理解的定理或证明，顺便说一句，数学中有不可理解的证明的历史。

turns.en: Like the four color theorem is a perfect example of this. It's like, okay, we just had a machine check a bunch of cases. There's no beauty in that. And so I think we're into a different phase of machine discovery.
turns.zh: 四色定理就是一个完美的例子。就像，好吧，我们只是让机器检查了一堆情况。这没什么美感。所以我认为我们进入了机器发现的不同阶段。

turns.en: I have some optimism that as models also get to better theory of mind, the ability to figure out what we as humans know and how to get us to follow them on the path to new understanding will also be paved. And so, for example, I'm a math person, but at some point in school I stopped learning math and then I did Math Academy and then I did like ChatGPT to help me learn new math. And so I just feel like the expectation for the rising tide of what knowledge you can expect people to understand will also be there.
turns.zh: 我有些乐观地认为，随着模型也获得更好的心理理论，即弄清楚我们人类知道什么以及如何让我们跟随它们走上新理解之路的能力也将被铺平。所以，例如，我是一个数学人，但在学校的某个时候我停止了学习数学，然后我用了 Math Academy，然后我用了 ChatGPT 来帮助我学习新的数学。所以我只是觉得，对知识涨潮的期望，即你可以期望人们理解什么，也会在那里。

turns.en: I think that this is a really important point and one of maybe the underappreciated benefits that I expect from and hope for and we're starting to see from this technology is helping people know more, understand more, understand each other better, understand the world better. And I think that there are technical mechanisms that can underlie the AI that's able to go and solve these problems, see all the connections between domains, but how does it actually communicate it to you? How do you understand it? And actually there's even connections to AI safety and alignment on having AI that we're able to understand what they're doing. And so there are techniques that we've been talking about since 2017, such as debate and iterative amplification, which are kind of two sides of a similar coin where you really think about if you have AIs that are solving problems that are just too hard for humans to check. And even for example, summarizing a book is an example of a task that's really hard to check, right? It's really hard to know is the summary any good unless you've read the whole book. And so if an AI just gives you a summary of a book and says this is the summary, is it a good summary or not a good summary? It's pretty hard unless you have another AI who is trying to prove that the summary is a bad summary. And so then if that AI comes back and says, "Hey, here's this paragraph in the book that I found that has a clearly very important plot point and that is not represented in the summary," you don't have to read the whole book to be like, "Oh yeah, that's actually a very good argument." And so you realize that there are ways to train the AI that are actually very aligned with having humans be able to have oversight, to be able to be in the driver's seat, which is a fundamental value, a fundamental thing that is important for the future from OpenAI's perspective, but also are very much aligned with what you're saying of can you make the results of an AI be something that means you learn something that is really tuned for the human rather than just sort of knowledge for some abstract knowledge sake.
turns.zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的点，也是我期望并希望从这项技术中看到的、我们开始看到的可能被低估的好处之一：帮助人们知道更多、理解更多、更好地相互理解、更好地理解世界。我认为有技术机制可以支撑 AI 能够解决这些问题，看到领域之间的所有联系，但它实际上如何与你沟通？你如何理解它？实际上，甚至与 AI 安全和 Alignment 也有联系，即让 AI 能够理解它们在做什么。所以有一些我们自 2017 年以来一直在讨论的技术，比如辩论和迭代放大，它们有点像同一枚硬币的两面，你真正考虑的是，如果你有 AI 正在解决人类难以检查的问题。甚至例如，总结一本书就是一个很难检查的任务，对吧？除非你读过整本书，否则很难知道摘要好不好。所以如果一个 AI 只是给你一本书的摘要并说这是摘要，它是好摘要还是不好摘要？这很难，除非你有另一个 AI 试图证明这个摘要是糟糕的摘要。然后如果那个 AI 回来说：“嘿，这是我在书中找到的一段，它有一个明显非常重要的情节点，而摘要中没有体现，”你不必读完整本书就能说：“哦，是的，这确实是一个很好的论点。”所以你意识到有办法训练 AI，这些方法实际上非常符合让人类能够监督、能够坐在驾驶座上，这是基本价值，从 OpenAI 的角度来看对未来很重要的事情，但也非常符合你所说的：你能让 AI 的结果成为让你学到东西的东西，真正为人类量身定制，而不是为了某种抽象的知识而知识。

transcript.sec: AI for Science and Drug Discovery

turns.en: For most people, advancements in math theory are still somewhat abstract, right? So there's like, "Wow, this is absolutely happening today." And then also, you know, AI for science, like there's a claim or a belief that it could solve all disease in some number of future years, right? How do you look forward like one step in terms of what we might see in advancements in between?
turns.zh: 对大多数人来说，数学理论的进步仍然有些抽象，对吧？所以会有“哇，这绝对在今天发生”的感觉。然后还有，你知道，AI for science，有一种说法或信念认为它可以在未来多少年内解决所有疾病，对吧？你如何向前看一步，即我们可能会看到什么中间进展？

turns.en: Well, I think that we've had a number of years in iterations of this technology to see the shape of what to expect. And I think that it's kind of like when you have an AI that is capable in a certain dimension. And if you understand the why it got capable in that dimension, then all other fields of human endeavor that have similar properties, you should also expect similar results. And so in my mind, why is mathematics something that we've managed to really transform in the way that we have had such incredible results? And part of it is that our AI is now at a certain level of capability and raw intelligence. Part of it is that you could think of it as that well, mathematics is checkable, but that's not quite true anymore, right? Like we really started with very checkable problems of here's a written arithmetic problem, there's some numeric answer, and so you have an AI that you can train to just like check if it got the answer right because we can very much just see is the answer that the AI is proposing the same as the actual answer? But for a proof, very different. Proofs are very hard to check. Is this actually accurate or not? A formalized proof, okay, yes, that is checkable, but natural language proof, which is what we're really producing here, much much more difficult. But the thing that actually I think is the core insight is really about data, right? It's that you can get lots of data in mathematics, you get lots of data in theoretical physics. Can you get lots of data in biology? That's obviously something very data bound, like very difficult. Now, fortunately, we also have been working on lots of techniques to be able to work with less data. And if you think about what that means is like, okay, we now have smart models that if there's something where there's a lot of data, and this is the fundamental physics of deep learning, right? Compute, data, algorithms equals capability, equals results. We're able to do it in these hard domains where people have spent hundreds of years of our smartest people all trying to solve the problem, and now the AI can solve it. Amazing. When you transfer that over to biology, and clearly what we want is drug discovery, all of these things that are like fundamental changes in biology and our understanding of it to improve quality of life, that's what we want to apply. The question will be and that is not yet resolved, do we have the data? Do we have the ability to get the data? And so I think that what will happen is that we will take these, and we're already doing this, where we take these models, these same techniques, and apply them in the biological domain. And there's some areas that will fall quickly, right? That we'll just see massive acceleration of things that used to be incredibly painful, now incredibly easy. But there will be other bottlenecks, and there'll be a question of, well, how do we alleviate those bottlenecks? And some of these, by the way, are not even really about deep biological theory. For example, regulatory filings. Huge bottleneck, right? It takes like a year to write up your whole sort of case for a clinical trial and all these things. And it's just like you can write those things in AI much more easily. And so I think that we have to look at every step of the drug discovery process. And there are going to be places where the fundamental data just does not exist.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为我们已经有了几年时间来迭代这项技术，以了解预期的形态。我认为这有点像当你有一个在某个维度上有能力的 AI。如果你理解它为什么在那个维度上有能力，那么所有其他具有类似属性的人类努力领域，你也应该期待类似的结果。所以在我看来，为什么数学是我们设法真正转变的领域，我们取得了如此不可思议的结果？部分原因是我们的 AI 现在处于一定的能力和原始智能水平。部分原因是你可以认为数学是可检查的，但这已经不太正确了，对吧？就像我们真正开始于非常可检查的问题，比如这里有一个书面算术问题，有一些数字答案，所以你可以训练 AI 来检查它是否答对了，因为我们可以非常直接地看到 AI 提出的答案是否与实际答案相同？但对于证明，非常不同。证明很难检查。这实际上准确吗？形式化的证明，好吧，是的，那是可检查的，但自然语言证明，这才是我们真正产生的，要困难得多。但我认为核心洞察实际上是关于数据，对吧？你可以在数学中获得大量数据，在理论物理中获得大量数据。你能在生物学中获得大量数据吗？这显然是受数据限制的，非常困难。现在，幸运的是，我们也一直在研究许多技术，以便能够用更少的数据工作。如果你想想这意味着什么，就像，好吧，我们现在有聪明的模型，如果有大量数据的东西，这是深度学习的基本物理，对吧？算力、数据、算法等于能力，等于结果。我们能够在这些困难的领域做到这一点，人们花了数百年时间，我们最聪明的人都在试图解决这个问题，现在 AI 可以解决它。太棒了。当你把它转移到生物学时，显然我们想要的是药物发现，所有这些生物学及其理解的根本性变化，以改善生活质量，这就是我们想要应用的。问题将是，而且尚未解决，我们有数据吗？我们有能力获取数据吗？所以我认为将会发生的是，我们将采取这些，我们已经这样做了，我们采取这些模型，这些相同的技术，并将它们应用于生物领域。有些领域会很快倒下，对吧？我们会看到曾经非常痛苦的事情现在变得非常容易，大规模加速。但会有其他瓶颈，问题将是，好吧，我们如何缓解这些瓶颈？顺便说一句，其中一些甚至不是真正关于深层生物学理论。例如，监管文件。巨大的瓶颈，对吧？写整个临床试验案例和所有这些事情需要大约一年时间。而你可以用 AI 更容易地写这些东西。所以我认为我们必须审视药物发现过程的每一步。而且会有一些地方根本数据不存在。

And so, I think that is the main distinction is really around cost. And we've seen this in ChatGPT, right? That ChatGPT, we put in a lot of effort to have the largest scale free tier and bringing things like memory to all of our free users was an incredible endeavor, like a real huge engineering effort. And it's just very easy to implement the same functionality at much higher cost for a very small number of people. And so, I think that what we're seeing in the personal assistant workspace is that there are going to be these different market segments where different amounts of compute are going to be expended fundamentally. And so, sometimes when there's different levels of compute, it then means that the product can look a little different, right? That it can be that there's just more functionality that's embedded in one versus the other. And there's of course different use cases. You think about things like payments and travel and things like that are much more for the consumer. But I don't think there's any fundamental difference, right? It's like really just like an AI that's doing things and it's just like happens to be like slight sort of pressure in one way or another. And so, one of the strengths of OpenAI is the fact that we have 1.2 billion consumers on ChatGPT and we have also a leading coding and enterprise business. And no one else has both in house. And so, a lot of our strategy is to say, let's unify these so we're not sort of competing on two fronts. It's really competing on one front. And I think that this is also the general direction of travel of AI is to blur the distinction between what is consumer, what is enterprise. We're going to have this renaissance of entrepreneurs. Like we're already seeing it. I mean, imagine you're seeing this very concretely. And I know people who are quitting their job to go start companies who say, I never would have done it if I didn't have an AI that I knew I could rely on that could take care of so much of the normal barriers to entry. And so, I think that we're going to see just like the distinctions have held for so long, I think they're going to change.

All of that needs to change and it was totally impossible to change with human software developers cuz there's so few. There's so few people who have this expertise in this very obscure thing of like you know, sort of knowing different packages and like different security techniques.
turns.zh: 我们之所以有那个世界，是因为一些物理规律，对吧？比如编写软件和编写可靠软件有多难。而且每个人都有供应链，但很少有公司审计他们的供应链，对吧？我们已经看到供应链漏洞，有人上传了一个恶意包，然后许多公司受到打击。所有这些都需要改变，而用人类软件开发人员完全不可能改变，因为人太少了。很少有人拥有这种非常 obscure 的专业知识，比如你知道，了解不同的包和不同的安全技术。

turns.en: Software now like Socket and others who will do this as an example where they'll scan through your open source supply chain and try and find vulnerabilities and identify them for you. Or, you know, there's the human element of it where a maintainer would suddenly take over a project and then install something that would be malicious relative to people then using that package. So, it's really interesting to see that shift in terms of the third-party ecosystem as well developing to support that process.
turns.zh: 现在像 Socket 这样的软件公司会做这样的事：扫描你的开源供应链，尝试发现漏洞并为你识别出来。或者，你知道，还有人为因素：维护者突然接管一个项目，然后安装一些对使用该包的人有害的东西。所以，看到第三方生态系统也在发展以支持这一过程，这种转变真的很有趣。

turns.en: OpenAI and others are doing in terms of this market.
turns.zh: OpenAI 和其他公司在这个市场上所做的。

turns.en: Exactly. I think it's so important. So, we're doing this with the community. We partner with companies like CrowdStrike and I think that it is again a coordinated response, but we really view it as a core priority for OpenAI to lead, right? For us to really because we have the frontier model, we have the peak intelligence model. Certainly in cybersecurity, we think that there is transformative potential for the good possible. But, that means that we as a company and we've been going through a security transition, right? That over the past couple months we've talked about safety security alignment of our development process, but we're also thinking about that for the world of how to really help the world become more fundamentally secure and help people through this whole period.
turns.zh: 正是如此。我认为这非常重要。我们正在与社区一起做这件事。我们与 CrowdStrike 等公司合作，我认为这又是一个协调一致的响应，但我们确实将其视为 OpenAI 引领的核心优先事项，对吧？对我们来说，因为我们拥有前沿模型，我们拥有巅峰智能模型。当然，在网络安全领域，我们认为有可能带来积极的变革潜力。但这意味着我们作为一个公司，我们一直在经历安全转型，对吧？在过去几个月里，我们谈到了开发过程中的安全、保障、对齐，但我们也在思考如何真正帮助世界变得更安全，帮助人们度过整个时期。

turns.en: One of the things about OpenAI is that it's always been very pro-human and very pro-human agency, human progress. Let's use AI to better everyone. I think the original premise of OpenAI was let's have something that can counterbalance other companies in terms of creating AI that can be used very broadly and universally in a positive way.
turns.zh: 关于 OpenAI 的一点是，它一直非常支持人类，非常支持人类能动性和人类进步。让我们用 AI 来改善每个人。我认为 OpenAI 最初的 premise 是，让我们拥有一些能够制衡其他公司的东西，创造出能够以积极方式广泛普遍使用的 AI。

turns.en: Has that ethos continued at OpenAI or how do you think about that in the context of the AI community?
turns.zh: 这种精神在 OpenAI 是否延续了，或者你在 AI 社区的背景下如何看待这一点？

turns.en: I think that ethos is very core to our mission, right? To ensure AGI benefits all of humanity. And the humanity there is very key. We think that humans should be firmly in the driver's seat, should have control over the future, and that this technology should amplify human agency.
turns.zh: 我认为这种精神是我们使命的核心，对吧？确保 AGI（通用人工智能）惠及全人类。其中“人类”非常关键。我们认为人类应该牢牢掌握方向盘，应该控制未来，这项技术应该增强人类能动性。

turns.en: Even as models surpass humans in capability.
turns.zh: 即使模型在能力上超越人类。

turns.en: And I think this is absolutely critical, right? That I think that the picture of and there Keep in mind these models are very jagged, right? That there are places where obviously these AIs are more capable than anyone today, right? Even GPT-4 knows far more than any person. But the thing that is so important, and I'm reminded for example of the There's the story of why Steve Jobs put the handle on the iMac, right? So that way people could feel that they could control the machine, right? That you can always pick it up and throw it out the window. And I think that the same spirit needs to apply to AI. The fact of the spirit of humans are in the driver's seat. That these like human judgment, human values, and maybe you should think of how humans will operate in certain fields, in certain dimensions in the future, whatever it is, is become more like CEOs, or like board members. But it's important that we have that level of agency, and that I think that we're going to build machines just like, you know, if you're a CEO, you're clearly going to have domain experts. You're clearly going to have teams that are going to have a knowledge across so many things and maybe even better ideas than you on many different axes. But fundamentally, the question is are you happy? Is this what you wanted? Is this what makes your life better? And that to me is something that we should all collectively it's not just about AI, it's about technology. Right? Technology is to lift up human civilization. It's the single most fundamental driver of improvement in quality of life and that is what we should be seeking from AI. That is the belief of OpenAI.
turns.zh: 我认为这绝对关键，对吧？我认为，要记住这些模型非常参差不齐，对吧？有些地方这些 AI 显然比今天任何人都更有能力，对吧？甚至 GPT-4 知道的比任何人都多。但非常重要的一点是，我想起了例如史蒂夫·乔布斯为什么在 iMac 上放一个把手的故事，对吧？这样人们就能感觉到他们可以控制机器，对吧？你总是可以把它捡起来扔出窗外。我认为同样的精神需要应用到 AI 上。人类在方向盘后的精神。这些像人类判断、人类价值观，也许你应该想想未来人类在某些领域、某些维度将如何运作，不管是什么，会变得更像 CEO，或者像董事会成员。但重要的是我们拥有那种程度的能动性，我认为我们将建造机器，就像，你知道，如果你是一个 CEO，你显然会有领域专家。你显然会有团队，他们拥有跨这么多领域的知识，甚至可能在许多方面有比你更好的想法。但根本问题是，你快乐吗？这是你想要的吗？这是让你的生活更好的东西吗？对我来说，这是我们所有人都应该集体思考的，不仅仅是关于 AI，而是关于技术。对吧？技术是为了提升人类文明。它是生活质量改善的最根本驱动力，这就是我们应该从 AI 中寻求的。这是 OpenAI 的信念。

turns.en: Thank you so much for doing this, Greg.
turns.zh: 非常感谢你接受这次采访，Greg。

turns.en: Yeah, thanks for your time. Thank you, both. Appreciate it.
turns.zh: 是的，感谢你们的时间。谢谢你们两位。非常感谢。
